title: Possible to make game with no code?
author: AuGKlasD
selftext:
Ive been exploring some options to make games using prompts only and came across [MakeGamesWithAI](https://makegameswithai.com).

What was interesting is that unlike any other options I tried it allowed you to select from a variety of remade gaming assets that are then inserted directly into your game.

It took a little work to get the hang of it at first, but after a few tries I was able to make this [zombie shooting game](https://makegameswithai.com/play/nTkzTlBQnv4u1BIos4jz) in a few minutes.

The games made also automatically come with pre-made leaderboards, so if other users are logged in you can compete for high scores in any game published.

What are some other options that users have tried? Any recommendations?

replies.author: atx78701
replies.body: I have had very good success with opus 4.5 in a cursor environment. There is pretty much nothing ive asked it to do that hasnt worked. It does do weird stuff sometimes, like it loves to store things in constants in code but Ill tell it to move it to fields in the database and it will do it.

comments.author: gabriel29ewui
comments.body: Look, I have a lot of experience with AI, and I'm telling you, coding everything with AI will be a terrible experience. I recommend using AI to help you create a game and studying programming. Even if you create projects like Flappy Bird, a cheap Vampire Survivor simulator, you won't get very far. As you refine the game, you'll create other bugs that you no know how to solve. These AI-generated games are great for quick prototypes to test ideas. I recommend using a less programming-intensive engine like GDevelop or Construct.

replies.author: AuGKlasD
replies.body: Thanks! Ive never tried either of those. Will give it a look!
